semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL uses explicit termination language: 'The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState' and 'The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState.' The word 'ends' and 'exits' establish that FinishState should be a stable termination point. The exact model facts show FinishState is not explicit-final (no edge to [*]) and has outgoing guard-free continuations. The rebuttal ('the existence of each completion endpoint does not establish stable termination') actually confirms the violation - having a transition TO FinishState does not make it a termination if it continues elsewhere. No supplied fact establishes FinishState as terminal.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: The NL requires HighwayMode to 'end' and UrbanMode to 'exit' at FinishState, implying stable termination; however FinishState is not explicit-final and its ancestor chain admits guard-free continuations (tr_0024, tr_0029), so neither operating scope obtains a stable termination boundary.

issues.basis: NL12 segment; exact_source_inventory.states (CollisionAvoidance parent=null line 37); FCSTM complete transition inventory (no incoming edge to CollisionAvoidance from root or any reachable state); verify_facts non_proved reachability refutations; inspection_equivalent_facts STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics; working_contract source_to_model mapping.
issues.expected: A path exists from the root initial state to the CollisionAvoidance composite, making it reachable and active as described by NL12.
issues.observed: The complete FCSTM transition inventory (56 transitions) contains no edge from root or any reachable state to CollisionAvoidance. Verify facts confirm reachability is refuted for state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83, state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:84, and state:collision_avoidance_active:line:85. The inspection diagnostics report STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for all three.
issues.reason: The source declares CollisionAvoidance at the same top level as AutonomousMode (both parent=null), and the NL uses present-tense system-state language. The complete closed transition inventory has no path from any reachable state to CollisionAvoidance, confirmed by deterministic verify facts. This is a structural reachability gap that makes the entire collision avoidance component dead code in the closed model.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL12 could be read as describing only the internal configuration of an independently-running subsystem that is not required to be entered from the main state machine's root. Under this reading, the internal initial entry (which exists) fully satisfies the obligation, and root reachability is not required.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance composite is unreachable from system root

issues.basis: NL12 segment; FCSTM transition:line:91 is the sole root entry; verify_facts check reachability:state:CollisionAvoidance:line:83 status=refuted; inspection diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL for lines 83, 84, 85; event_consumers show reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for both collision avoidance events; reachable_state_count=14 excludes all CollisionAvoidance states.
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance is reachable from the machine root, allowing its collision avoidance activation and deactivation behavior to be operationally executed.
issues.observed: The machine root has exactly one entry edge ([*] -> AutonomousMode, transition:line:91). No entry edge exists to CollisionAvoidance. Verify_facts refutes reachability for all three CollisionAvoidance states. Inspection diagnostics confirm STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL. The two collision avoidance events have declared consumers but zero reachable consumers (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostics).
issues.reason: The NL establishes CollisionAvoidance as an operational system with specific activation conditions, but the closed model provides no path from the machine root to this composite. This is a distinct root-reachability property from the owner-local initial_entry (which is satisfied) and from event-consumer coverage (which is also affected but is a separate property).
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state. It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionAvoidance might be intended as an independently deployed component with its own external entry point not modeled in this state machine. However, the NL presents it as part of the same operational system without indicating external activation, and the PlantUML source places it at the same top level as AutonomousMode within a single diagram, implying co-activation.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance composite permanently unreachable from machine root

issues.basis: NL6 segment; FCSTM transition:line:40 (FinishState -> [*] on auto_finished_true, effect R45RouteToken=29), transition:line:75 (HighwayMode -> [*] guard R45RouteToken==29), transition:line:90 (AutonomousMode -> AutonomousMode self-loop guard R45RouteToken==29), transition:line:77 ([*] -> HighwayMode guard R45RouteToken==29), transition:line:24 ([*] -> FinishState guard R45RouteToken==29, effect R45RouteToken=0). The complete cycle path is verified in the closed model topology.
issues.expected: Once HighwayMode reaches FinishState via auto_finished=true, the termination is stable: the system does not re-enter HighwayMode or continue operational behavior from FinishState.
issues.observed: FinishState has an outgoing transition on auto_finished_true (transition:line:40) that sets R45RouteToken=29 and performs a local exit from HighwayMode. At the AutonomousMode level, the self-loop transition (transition:line:90, guard R45RouteToken==29) re-enters AutonomousMode, which then takes the guarded entry to HighwayMode (transition:line:77, guard R45RouteToken==29), and HighwayMode enters FinishState again (transition:line:24, guard R45RouteToken==29, effect R45RouteToken=0). This creates a cycle: FinishState -> exit -> re-enter FinishState, meaning termination is not stable.
issues.reason: The termination contract requires HighwayMode to end stably at FinishState. The closed model allows FinishState to exit and re-enter itself through the R45RouteToken=29 mechanism, violating the stability requirement of termination. No frozen predicate directly expresses stable termination (absence of re-entry cycles at a terminal state), so predicate_id is null.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The re-entry at FinishState requires auto_finished_true to fire a second time at FinishState, which might never occur in practice if the condition is one-shot. Additionally, the cycle could be interpreted as a compiler mechanism for the source-level AutonomousMode -> FinishState transition rather than an author-intended behavioral loop. However, the closed model as constructed does permit this cycle, and stable termination requires the terminal state to be absorbing.
issues.title: HighwayMode termination not stable: FinishState re-enters via R45RouteToken=29 cycle

issues.basis: NL10 segment; FCSTM transitions:line:56 (straight -> [*] auto_finished_true, R45RouteToken=21), transition:line:71 (UrbanMode -> HighwayMode guard token==21), transition:line:22 (HighwayMode [*] -> FinishState guard token==21), transition:line:40 (FinishState -> [*] auto_finished_true, R45RouteToken=29), transition:line:90 (AutonomousMode self-loop guard token==29), transition:line:77 ([*] -> HighwayMode guard token==29), transition:line:24 (HighwayMode [*] -> FinishState guard token==29). The termination path from UrbanMode reaches the same unstable FinishState.
issues.expected: Once UrbanMode exits to FinishState via auto_finished=true, the termination is stable: the system does not re-enter any operating mode from FinishState.
issues.observed: UrbanMode exits to FinishState via straight -> [*] (transition:line:56, R45RouteToken=21) or intersection -> [*] (transition:line:58, R45RouteToken=23), then UrbanMode -> HighwayMode (transition:line:71 or 72), then HighwayMode [*] -> FinishState (transition:line:22 or 23). Once at FinishState, the same auto_finished_true exit cycle applies: transition:line:40 sets R45RouteToken=29, the AutonomousMode self-loop (transition:line:90) re-enters, and HighwayMode re-enters at FinishState (transition:line:77, transition:line:24). Termination is not stable.
issues.reason: The UrbanMode termination contract designates FinishState as the stable ending target. The closed model permits FinishState to exit and re-enter itself through the R45RouteToken=29 mechanism, the same cycle identified for HighwayMode termination. This is a distinct termination obligation for UrbanMode even though it shares the same target state and cycle.
issues.requirement_quote: The system exits the UrbanMode state by transitioning to FinishState once `auto_finished=true` is satisfied.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The UrbanMode-to-FinishState path uses R45RouteToken=21/23 (not 29), and the re-entry cycle at FinishState requires a second auto_finished_true event. If auto_finished is a one-shot condition that cannot re-fire, the cycle is theoretically unreachable. However, the closed model does not enforce one-shot semantics, and the structural cycle exists in the transition graph.
issues.title: UrbanMode termination not stable: designated FinishState target re-enters via R45RouteToken cycle

issues.basis: NL12 activation conditions and NL13 deactivation conditions; verify_facts check event-consumer:pedestrian_detected... status=refuted (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:87], reachable=[]); verify_facts check event-consumer:front_inactive... status=refuted (consumer_transition_refs=[transition:line:88], reachable=[]); inspection_equivalent_facts event_consumers confirm reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] for both.
issues.expected: Both the collision avoidance activation event and the deactivation event have at least one consumer transition reachable from the machine root within the CollisionAvoidance scope.
issues.observed: Both events have exactly one declared consumer each (transition:line:87 for activation, transition:line:88 for deactivation), but both consumers are in unreachable states. Verify_facts refutes event-consumer for both events with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. Inspection diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE confirms no reachable consumer exists.
issues.reason: The NL establishes that collision avoidance events must be consumable for the system to operate. Deterministic facts confirm that while consumer transitions exist, none is reachable from the machine root. This is a distinct property from root reachability of the composite: even if a different entry mechanism were added, the specific consumer coverage obligation for these events would need to be verified independently. No frozen predicate directly expresses event-consumer-coverage-with-reachability, so predicate_id is null.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Event consumer coverage is a consequence of the root reachability failure rather than an independent structural defect. If CollisionAvoidance were made reachable, both consumers would immediately become reachable. However, the protocol requires treating root reachability and event-consumer coverage as independent frontier properties, and this candidate preserves the operational consequence that these specific events can never be consumed regardless of the root cause classification.
issues.title: Collision avoidance events have declared but no reachable consumers in operating scope
